Given the reliance on existing serialized attention, standard losses, and beam search, stronger controlled comparisons are needed.

Graph and point matching methods require substantive changes to support many-to-one lane-to-road assignments, while trajectory methods process numerous overlapping paths. Enumerating and duplicating all root-to-leaf paths can require exponentially many tokens even in an acyclic graph, contradicting Appendix F.1's polynomial worst-case bound. Handling cycles, limiting path enumeration, and measuring runtime as branching increases are necessary to substantiate the scalability claims.

Novelty and baseline fairness need stronger treatment. Spatial serialization and grouped attention closely resemble existing serialized point-transformer designs, while PTv3 appears only as an insufficiently documented ablation baseline. The graph-, point-, and trajectory-matching methods require substantial adaptation to this many-to-one task, but those adaptations and tuning procedures are not adequately described. Strong task-matched neural baselines on the noisy test sets would better establish the contribution.

The evaluation protocol limits the independence of the test results. Validation and test use the same underlying scenes and annotations with different perception inputs, so they constitute clean/noisy evaluations of the same held-out geography. The paper does not explain how model selection avoids adapting to these shared scenes. Appendix D.1 additionally excludes 40 scenes for low-quality predictions without specifying a reproducible filtering rule or reporting results with those failures included.

Important reproducibility details remain missing despite the extensive appendix. These include construction of predicted lane connectivity, reconciliation of conflicting labels across overlapping decoded paths, and precise baseline implementations. Code and annotations are promised only upon publication. Training specifications also disagree on weight decay: 0.05 in the main text versus 0.005 in Appendix I. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported for the small ablation and transfer differences.
